output.headline: Moves about $1.1M in unclaimed payment funds from stale-dated checks into the General Fund
output.sourceIssueCandidate: The text lists two check counts (2,690 and 2680) and two cumulative amounts ($1,104,758.00 and $1,069,434.46), which looks like an unresolved edit; the larger amount was used here.
output.summary: The Board adopts a resolution moving money from old district checks that were never cashed (stale-dated warrants) into the General Fund, as California law allows, for 2019-20 as of May 31, 2020. The official text lists two counts of checks (2,690 and 2680) and two amounts ($1,104,758.00 and $1,069,434.46), so the exact figure is unclear from the text alone.

output.headline: Accepts $750,000 from the Stupski Foundation for college and career advising support
output.summary: The Board approves a grant from the Stupski Foundation to support coordination with community-based organizations and advising professional development in the High School Linked Learning Office. The grant period is February 1, 2020 through January 31, 2023.

output.headline: Adds $14,700 to The Integral Group's contract for the Cole Administration Center project
output.summary: The Board amends a contract with The Integral Group, Inc. so it pursues CHPS green-building certification instead of LEED v4 and provides additional building-systems and commissioning work for the data center and multipurpose building. The contract limit rises from $57,500 to $72,200, paid from Measure J bond funds.

output.headline: Hires HERTZ Environmental for $25,500 of stormwater pollution planning at the Cole Administration Center
output.summary: The Board approves a contract with HERTZ Environmental, Inc. to prepare a Storm Water Pollution Prevention Plan and help the district comply with the state Construction General Permit for stormwater runoff at the Cole Administration Center project. Work starts August 13, 2020 and is scheduled to last through December 31, 2023, paid from Measure J bond funds.

output.headline: Adds $10,000 for Jensen Hughes fire and intrusion alarm testing at the Fremont construction project
output.summary: The Board amends a contract with Jensen Hughes for additional site visits to witness pre-testing and final testing of the fire alarm and intrusion alarm systems for Increment 2 of the Fremont New Construction Project. The added amount includes a $5,250 contingency, and the contract limit rises from $76,430 to $86,430, paid from Measure J bond funds.

output.headline: Adds $40,750 and extends Verde Design's Emerson softball field contract to June 2021
output.sourceIssueCandidate: The text says 'the former' (the District) provides reimbursable DSA fees 'to latter' (Verde Design), which appears to reverse the roles of the parties.
output.summary: The Board amends a contract with Verde Design for the Emerson Elementary School softball field project, covering reimbursable fees paid to the Division of the State Architect (DSA), the state agency that reviews school construction plans. The added amount includes a $15,000 contingency, the limit rises from $266,360 to $307,110, and the end date moves from December 31, 2020 to June 21, 2021. It is paid from Measure J bond funds.

output.headline: Adds $147,000 to Byrens Kim Design Works' contract for the Madison Park Academy expansion
output.sourceIssueCandidate: The title says 'Professional Development' but the action text describes 'Professional Services' (design and construction administration).
output.summary: The Board amends a contract with Byrens Kim Design Works for additional site design for the Capistrano Driveway and West Parking lot to address structural construction errors, plus extra construction administration for the longer construction period at Madison Park Academy. The contract limit rises from $2,695,870 to $2,842,870, paid from Measure J bond funds.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $35,500 for DCG Strategies to manage two former school-related properties
output.summary: The Board ratifies a contract with DCG Strategies, Inc. for asset management and real property services on the former Edward Shands Adult Education Center and the former Tilden Child Development Center site. The contract runs June 25, 2020 through March 15, 2021, and the work began before the Board's vote. It is paid from the Special Reserve for Capital Facilities fund.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $7,500 for Heafey Commercial to manage two former child development sites
output.summary: The Board ratifies a contract with Heafey Commercial for asset management and real property services on the former Piedmont and former Webster Child Development Center sites. The contract runs June 25, 2020 through December 31, 2021, and the work began before the Board's vote. It is paid from the Special Reserve for Capital Facilities fund.

output.headline: Expands student data sharing with the Oakland Housing Authority at no cost
output.summary: This amends an existing memorandum of understanding (a partnership agreement) between the district and the Housing Authority of the City of Oakland. The district would share student directory information, combined test-result data, and information on students' device and internet access for students in households that get housing assistance. All other terms stay the same, and there is no fiscal impact.

vendor.name: Housing Authority of the City of Oakland

output.headline: Ratifies $19.4M in April 2020 payroll checks and direct deposits
output.summary: The Board ratifies payroll for April 1 to 30, 2020: 901 printed checks and 6,997 direct deposits totaling $19,437,448.42. This is after-the-fact approval of routine employee pay for fiscal year 2019-20.

output.headline: Ratifies $19.96M in May 2020 payroll checks and direct deposits
output.summary: The Board ratifies payroll for May 1 to 31, 2020: 932 printed checks and 7,016 direct deposits totaling $19,962,670.50. This is after-the-fact approval of routine employee pay for fiscal year 2019-20.

output.headline: Approves $16.2M in June 2020 payroll checks and direct deposits
output.summary: The Board approves payroll for June 1 to 30, 2020: 688 printed checks and 7,034 direct deposits totaling $16,181,082.61. This is routine employee pay for fiscal year 2019-20.

output.headline: Approves $25.4M in April 2020 checks paid to vendors and suppliers
output.summary: The Board approves accounts payable checks for April 1 to 30, 2020: 802 printed checks totaling $25,400,834.92. These are the district's routine payments for goods and services in fiscal year 2019-20.

output.headline: Approves $29.6M in May 2020 checks paid to vendors and suppliers
output.summary: The Board approves accounts payable checks for May 1 to 31, 2020: 698 printed checks totaling $29,578,441.90. These are the district's routine payments for goods and services in fiscal year 2019-20.

output.headline: Approves $39.8M in June 2020 checks paid to vendors and suppliers
output.summary: The Board approves accounts payable checks for June 1 to 30, 2020: 1,153 printed checks totaling $39,769,105.02. These are the district's routine payments for goods and services in fiscal year 2019-20.

output.headline: Lets the district borrow between its own funds as needed for cash flow in 2020-21
output.summary: The Board adopts a resolution allowing the district to temporarily borrow between its eligible funds during fiscal year 2020-21 to manage cash flow, and to repay those loans, as state Education Code Section 42603 allows. No dollar amount is stated.

output.headline: Approves the 2020-21 course offerings for Oakland Adult and Career Education
output.summary: The Board adopts a resolution approving the course offerings of the Oakland Adult and Career Education program for the 2020-2021 school year. The item states no fiscal impact.

output.headline: Accepts $24,860.55 from Intel via Oakland Public Education Fund for a McClymonds counselor
output.summary: The Board accepts a grant passed through the Oakland Public Education Fund from the Intel Corporation. It fully funds the Remote Learning and College Counselor position at McClymonds High School for the 2020-2021 school year.

output.headline: Adopts updated salary schedules for substitute teachers in the Oakland Education Association unit
output.summary: The Board adopts a resolution setting salary schedules for substitute certificated (teaching) positions covered by the Oakland Education Association (OEA). It lists past raises dating back to 2007, plus daily rates for short- and long-term substitutes and a 3% increase for child development and adult education substitutes effective January 1, 2019 and January 1, 2020. No total dollar amount is stated.

output.headline: Approves a resolution agreement with the U.S. Office for Civil Rights on a disability discrimination case
output.summary: The Board approves a resolution agreement with the U.S. Department of Education's Office for Civil Rights to resolve Case No. 09-19-1027, which concerned alleged discrimination based on disability. The item states no dollar amount or details of the terms.

vendor.name: U.S. Department of Education, Office for Civil Rights

output.headline: Accepts $70,000 from Intel via Oakland Public Education Fund for Oakland Tech's Computer Academy
output.summary: The Board accepts a grant passed through the Oakland Public Education Fund from the Intel Corporation. It supports the Computer Academy Director's salary at Oakland Technical High School for the 2019-2020 school year, a period that began before the Board's vote.

output.headline: Authorizes up to $23M for nonpublic schools and agencies serving special education students in 2020-21
output.summary: The Board adopts a resolution approving new master agreements and individual service agreements with nonpublic, nonsectarian schools and agencies (nonpublic school/agency, or NPS/NPA) that serve students in special education. The total across all of these agreements for fiscal year 2020-21 cannot exceed $23,000,000.

output.headline: Pays PLS Surveys $10,200 for a boundary survey of the former John Swett Elementary site
output.summary: The Board approves a contract with PLS Surveys, Inc. for a boundary survey and parcel map to subdivide the former John Swett Elementary School site, part of the Tilden Project. The contract runs August 27, 2020 through March 31, 2021 and is paid from the Special Reserve for Capital Facilities fund.

output.headline: Accepts a $1.42M K12 Strong Workforce grant through the Cabrillo Community College District
output.summary: The Board approves an agreement under which Oakland Unified accepts a $1,416,149 grant to support its K12 Strong Workforce Program, which funds career technical education pathways. The grant is handled through the High School Linked Learning Office and runs July 1, 2020 through December 31, 2022. Cabrillo Community College District acts as fiscal agent for the California Community Colleges Chancellor's Office.

output.headline: Adopts Personnel Report No. 2021-0001 from the Talent/Human Resources Department
output.summary: The Board adopts the Human Resources Department's personnel report, which lists staffing actions. The agenda text gives no dollar amounts or details in the item itself.

output.headline: Authorizes on-site internships and career pathway programs during 2020-21 shelter-in-place orders
output.summary: The Board adopts a resolution allowing on-site internships and career pathway programs for the 2020-21 school year, as long as they follow the COVID-19 shelter-in-place orders in effect. No dollar amount is stated.

output.headline: Ratifies $18,000 yearly lease of two Castlemont High buildings to Kidango
output.summary: The Board ratifies a lease letting Kidango, Inc. use Buildings H and I at Castlemont High School for an early childhood education and family support program for low-income children in the Castlemont community. Kidango pays a one-time $18,000 plus $18,000 in annual rent for the term July 8, 2020 through June 30, 2021, and the lease began before the Board's vote.
